chapter_title: Open File Formats and Version Control
learning_objective: The learner will examine the history of a small repository to find the commit that answers each of six questions, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: graph-model **sim-id:** git-history-explorer
**Library:** vis-network
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze
**Bloom Verb:** examine
**Learning Objective:** The learner will examine the history of a small repository to find the commit that answers each of six questions, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Version Control, Git (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** In quiz mode the learner clicks the commit that answers a question. A click is correct when it matches the Correct commit column in Content. Mastery is at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. Clicking commits in explore mode is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A merge commit is the same as the changes it combines. (2) A branch is a separate copy of the files. (3) The history cannot show who made a change. **Instructional Rationale:** Examining a history is an Analyze-level action, because the learner must read the parts, the messages and the structure, to find which one answers a question. A graph shows the branch and the merge as shape, so the learner sees what the words describe. **Content:** The graph has 8 nodes, one per commit, and 8 edges. Each edge points from a commit to its parent, the commit that came before it. Commit c7 is a merge commit and has two parents, c6 and c5. The repository is a made-up practice set called Fraction Practice Set, and the authors are made up. Clicking a node highlights its parents and children and shows its details. | Commit | Author | Date | Message | Files changed | Branch | Parents | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | c1 | Priya Shah | 2026-09-01 | Add first draft of the fraction problems | problems.md | main | none | | c2 | Priya Shah | 2026-09-03 | Add an answer key | answers.md | main | c1 | | c3 | Sam Okafor | 2026-09-10 | Fix the answer to problem 7 | answers.md | main | c2 | | c4 | Dana Reyes | 2026-09-12 | Start alt text work: describe the two number-line images | problems.md | alt-text | c3 | | c5 | Dana Reyes | 2026-09-13 | Add alt text to two more images | problems.md | alt-text | c4 | | c6 | Priya Shah | 2026-09-14 | Define denominator where it first appears | problems.md | main | c3 | | c7 | Priya Shah | 2026-09-15 | Merge the alt-text branch into main | problems.md | main | c6 and c5 | | c8 | Priya Shah | 2026-09-16 | Add CHANGELOG.md listing the changes | CHANGELOG.md | main | c7 | The six questions, in this order: | # | Question shown to the learner | Correct commit | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Which commit first added an answer key? | c2 | Its message says it added an answer key, and it changed answers.md. | | 2 | Which commit corrected a wrong answer? | c3 | Its message says it fixed the answer to problem 7. | | 3 | Which commit began the alt text work? | c4 | It is the first commit on the alt-text branch and its message names the number-line images. | | 4 | Which commit brought the alt text work into the main line? | c7 | It is the merge commit, and it has two parents, c6 and c5. | | 5 | Which commit created the first list of changes? | c8 | It added CHANGELOG.md. | | 6 | Which commit defined the word denominator? | c6 | Its message says it defined denominator where it first appears. | **Provenance:** The repository, authors, dates, and messages are made up for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative example". The terms follow the chapter section "Git". **Rules:** Each question has exactly one correct commit. Clicking a branch label or the background during the quiz counts as a wrong attempt. The sim offers buttons to zoom and does not zoom with the mouse wheel. **Learner Activity:** 1. In explore mode the learner clicks each commit and reads its author, date, message, and files changed. 2. In quiz mode the sim shows question 1 above the graph. 3. The learner clicks the commit that answers it. 4. If the first click is wrong, the sim says so and the learner tries once more. If the second click is also wrong, the sim reveals the commit and the Why text. 5. After question 6 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 6 questions in the fixed order, two attempts each. Only a correct first click counts as evidence. Correct: "Correct: [commit]. [Why]". First wrong click: "Not quite. Read the commit messages again." Second wrong click: "The answer is [commit]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 6 correct on the first attempt". At 5 or more it adds "You can read a history." Below 5 it lists the questions the learner missed. **Starting State:** The graph with all 8 commits visible, explore mode active, and the prompt "Click a commit to see what changed." **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's terms are repository, commit, branch, and merge. The chapter says a history records an author, a date, and a message for every change.
